newsitem.title: FRANCE: Greens vote to join French left-wing government.
newsitem.headline: Greens vote to join French left-wing government.

text.p: France's ecologist Greens voted in principle on Monday to join a left-wing government headed by Socialist prime minister-designate Lionel Jospin.

"We want to go all the way in our participation...and if possible to have more than one minister," Greens leader Dominique Voynet told reporters after the party's national council voted almost unanimously to join the government.
True to their principles opposing the holding of more than one political office, the Greens said none of their eight members of the new National Assembly would take a cabinet job.
That ruled out Voynet, the party's most charismatic leader.
Political sources said Jospin was considering appointing Marie-Christine Blandin, who has been president of the Nord-Pas de Calais regional council since 1992, as the first Green minister.
Voynet said she hoped he Greens would get not just an environment ministry with enlarged powers but also a social portfolio that could deal with reducing working hours and with women's rights.
The environmentalist party entered the National Assembly for the first time on Sunday, although it has won seats in European Parliament, regional and municipal elections in France.
